full_judgment:
Md Bazlur Rahman, J: This civil revision has been directed at the instance of the preemptee-appellant-petitioner under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and order dated 8-2-2011 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 55 of 2009 affirming the judgment and order dated 29-4-2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chitalmari in Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2001 allowing the preemption filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 4. The summarized facts leading to the application for revision are that pre-emptor-opposite party Nod, Profulla Kumar Bagchi, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 2001 against the pre-emptee appellant petitioner and others under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for getting the land in dispute preempted in his favour. The case of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 was that the disputed land appertaining to SA Khatian No.2125 originally belonged to Piary Bagchi, Baidya Nath Bagchi and others. Piary Bagchi died leaving behind the solitary son being the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 and, as such, he is a co-sharer by inheritance to the disputed holding. Another recorded tenant Baidya Nath Bagchi after his demise was succeeded by 4 sons being 2-5 opposite parties. Opposite party No.2 Bishnu Bagchi transferred the disputed land measuring an area of 26 decimals by virtue of an instrument of sale dated 4-9-2000 to pre-emptee-appellant petitioner wherein it was stated that the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 would possess the entire amount of disputed land from plot No.5853 recorded in SA Khatian No.2125. The pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 was totally unconversant of the transfer in question of which he first came to know on 5-4-2001 from Omar Ali Kazi. Subsequently, he obtained the certified copy of the disputed kabala from the concerned office and thereafter filed the preemption case on 24-4-2001.
